questions.title: Rectangle Area with a Class
questions.description:
OOP starts by bundling data and behavior together. Define a class Rectangle with two fields length and width and a method area() that returns length * width. In main, read the two values, store them in a Rectangle object, and print the area returned by the object's method.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated numbers: length and width.

Output Format:
Print one line: the rectangle area rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
0 < length, width <= 10000

questions.title: Student Profile Display
questions.description:
Define a class Student with three fields: name (String), rollNo (int) and marks (int). Give the class a method display() that prints the three fields, one per line. In main, read the values, fill a Student object, and call display().

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated values: name rollNo marks (name is one word).

Output Format:
Line 1: Name: <name>
Line 2: Roll: <rollNo>
Line 3: Marks: <marks>

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 50, 1 <= rollNo <= 9999, 0 <= marks <= 100

questions.title: Private Counter Taps
questions.description:
Encapsulation keeps a field safe inside a class. Define a class Counter with a private int field count starting at 0, a method increment() that adds 1 to count, and a method getCount() that returns count. In main, read n, create one Counter object, call increment() exactly n times, and print the final value through getCount().

Input Format:
A single line with one integer n.

Output Format:
Print one line: the counter value after n increments.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000

questions.title: Book Summary Line
questions.description:
Define a class Book with private fields title, author and price. Provide a method setDetails(String t, String a, double p) to fill them and a method summary() that returns the line: title by author costs P.PP (price with 2 decimals). In main, read title, author and price, fill the book through setDetails, and print book.summary().

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated values: title author price (title and author are single words).

Output Format:
Print one line exactly as returned by summary(): <title> by <author> costs <price with 2 decimals>.

Constraints:
1 <= title, author length <= 50, 0 <= price <= 100000

questions.title: Circle Circumference Class
questions.description:
Define a class Circle with a field radius and a method circumference() that returns 2 * Math.PI * radius. In main, read the radius, store it in a Circle object, and print the circumference returned by the object's method.

Input Format:
A single line with one number, the radius r.

Output Format:
Print one line: the circumference rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
0 < r <= 10000

questions.title: Dog Extends Animal Demo
questions.description:
Inheritance lets one class reuse another's members. Define a class Animal with a field name and a method eat() that prints: <name> eats food. Define a class Dog that extends Animal and adds a method bark() that prints: <name> barks. In main, read the dog's name, store it in a Dog object, then call eat() (inherited from Animal) and bark() (defined in Dog itself).

Input Format:
A single line with one word: the dog's name.

Output Format:
Line 1: <name> eats food
Line 2: <name> barks

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 50

questions.title: Bank Deposit Only Account
questions.description:
A new bank account starts empty. Define a class BankAccount with a private double field balance starting at 0.0, a method deposit(double amount) that adds to the balance, and a method getBalance() that returns it. In main, read n and then n deposit amounts, perform the deposits in order on one account object, and print the final balance.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n space-separated deposit amounts.

Output Format:
Print one line: the final balance rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= deposit amount <= 100000

questions.title: Employee Profile Card
questions.description:
An office portal prints a small profile card for every employee. Define a class Employee with fields name (String), department (String) and salary (double), plus a method printCard() that prints three lines: Employee: <name>, then Department: <department>, then Salary: <salary with 2 decimals>. In main, read the values, fill the object, and call printCard().

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated values: name department salary.

Output Format:
Line 1: Employee: <name>
Line 2: Department: <department>
Line 3: Salary: <salary with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1 <= name, department length <= 50, 0 <= salary <= 1000000

questions.title: Point Distance from Origin
questions.description:
A well-designed class hides how a result is computed. Define a class Point with fields x and y and a method distanceFromOrigin() that returns Math.sqrt(x * x + y * y). In main, read the coordinates, store them in a Point object, and print whatever the object's method returns. main only asks the object for the distance; the formula stays hidden inside the class.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated numbers: x and y.

Output Format:
Print one line: the distance from the origin rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
-1000 <= x, y <= 1000

questions.title: Pet Voices via Base Reference
questions.description:
Two different pet objects answer the same call differently. Define a base class Pet with a field name and a method speak() that returns some default sound. Define class Dog extends Pet with speak() returning Woof, and class Cat extends Pet with speak() returning Meow. Read two pets (type then name each), keep both objects in Pet variables, and for each print: <name> says <what speak() returns>.

Input Format:
A single line with four space-separated tokens: type1 name1 type2 name2, where each type is Dog or Cat.

Output Format:
Line 1: <name1> says <sound1>
Line 2: <name2> says <sound2>

Constraints:
Each type is Dog or Cat; 1 <= name length <= 50
questions.sampleoutput1:
Tommy says Woof
Mani says Meow
questions.sampleoutput2:
Bella says Meow
Rocky says Woof
questions.output1:
Rex says Woof
Ace says Woof
questions.output2:
Tom says Meow
Sara says Meow
questions.output3:
Buddy says Woof
Luna says Meow
questions.inputconstrains: Each type is Dog or Cat; 1 <= name length <= 50

questions.title: Abstract Shape Area Chooser
questions.description:
An abstract class states what every shape must do without saying how. Define an abstract class Shape with an abstract method area(). Define Circle extends Shape (field radius, area = Math.PI * radius * radius) and Rectangle extends Shape (fields width and height, area = width * height). Read one shape description, build the matching object through a Shape reference, and print its area. Writing new Shape() directly would not even compile, because abstract classes cannot be instantiated.

Input Format:
A single line: either circle r OR rect w h.

Output Format:
Print one line: the area rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
0 < r, w, h <= 10000

questions.title: Vehicle Family Describe
questions.description:
Inheritance is about reuse: a Car already has everything a Vehicle has, then adds its own touch. Define class Vehicle with a method show() printing: I am a vehicle. Define class Car extends Vehicle with an extra method wheels() printing: I have 4 wheels. Read n vehicle descriptions; for each Vehicle print only show(), and for each Car print show() (the inherited method) followed by wheels() (its own method).

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n space-separated words, each Car or Vehicle.

Output Format:
For each vehicle in input order, print its lines as described above.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100
questions.sampleoutput1:
I am a vehicle
I have 4 wheels
I am a vehicle
questions.output1:
I am a vehicle
I have 4 wheels
I am a vehicle
I have 4 wheels
I am a vehicle
questions.output2:
I am a vehicle
I have 4 wheels
questions.output3:
I am a vehicle
I am a vehicle

questions.title: Shape Array Base Dispatch
questions.description:
One array, many shapes: the power of a base type. Define an abstract class Shape with an abstract method area(), plus Circle (field radius) and Rectangle (fields width, height) subclasses. Read n shapes, store every object in a Shape[] array, then walk the array once calling shapes[i].area() and print each result. The same line of code handles circles and rectangles.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by the n shape descriptions, each written as circle r or rect w h, in order.

Output Format:
Print n lines: each shape's area rounded to exactly 2 decimal places, in input order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 < r, w, h <= 10000

questions.title: Manager Salary Inheritance
questions.description:
A Manager is an Employee with something extra. Define class Employee with fields name (String) and salary (double) and a method totalPay() that returns salary. Define class Manager extends Employee adding field bonus and overriding totalPay() to return salary + bonus. For each staff record print: <name> earns <total with 2 decimals>.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n records as tokens: role name salary [bonus], where role is Employee (no bonus token) or Manager (a bonus token follows salary).

Output Format:
Print n lines: <name> earns <totalPay with 2 decimals>, in input order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= salary, bonus <= 1000000
questions.input1: 3 Employee Om 1000 Employee Max 2000 Manager Boss 3000 3000
questions.output1:
Om earns 1000.00
Max earns 2000.00
Boss earns 6000.00

questions.title: Bank Withdraw Validation
questions.description:
With private data, the only way in is through the object's own rules. Define class BankAccount with a private double field balance, a method deposit(double amount) that adds it, a method withdraw(double amount) that subtracts only when amount <= balance and otherwise prints Insufficient funds, and a method getBalance(). Read n operations, apply them in order on one account, and print the final balance at the end.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n operations, each written as the letter D or W followed by the amount.

Output Format:
Print Insufficient funds immediately for every rejected withdrawal (in order), then one final line: the balance rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= amount <= 100000
questions.blacklist: public double balance, public int balance

questions.title: Payment Method Dispatcher
questions.description:
One checkout, many payment kinds. Define base class Payment with a method pay(int amount) that prints: Paid <amount>. Define CardPayment extends Payment overriding pay to print: Paid <amount> by card, and CashPayment extends Payment overriding pay to print: Paid <amount> in cash. For each transaction, read the kind and amount, hold the object in a Payment variable, and call pay: the object itself decides the message.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n transactions as tokens: kind amount, where kind is card or cash.

Output Format:
Print n lines, one per transaction in input order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= amount <= 100000
questions.sampleoutput1:
Paid 500 by card
Paid 200 in cash
questions.output1:
Paid 10 by card
Paid 20 in cash
Paid 30 by card
questions.output3:
Paid 5 in cash
Paid 7 in cash

questions.title: Abstract Notification System
questions.description:
A notification hub sends the same command to different channels. Define an abstract class Notification with an abstract method send(String message). Define EmailNotification extends Notification where send prints: EMAIL: <message>, and SMSNotification extends Notification where send prints: SMS: <message>. Read n notification lines, dispatch each through a Notification reference, and finish with the two count lines.

Input Format:
First line: one integer n. Then n lines, each: email <message> or sms <message> (the message may contain spaces).

Output Format:
One output line per notification in order, then the line Email total: <count of email notifications> and the line SMS total: <count of sms notifications>.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= message length <= 200

questions.title: Zoo Animal Feeder
questions.description:
The zookeeper calls eat() on every animal and each species answers its own way. Define base class Animal with a method eat(int units) that prints: Animal eats <units> kg. Define Lion extends Animal overriding eat to print: Lion munches <units> kg of meat, and Elephant extends Animal overriding eat to print: Elephant munches <units> kg of hay. Process n feeding orders through Animal references and report the total food served.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n feedings as tokens: kind units, where kind is Lion or Elephant.

Output Format:
One line per feeding in input order, then a final line: Total food: <sum of units> kg.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= units <= 1000

Elephant munches 1 kg of hay

Elephant munches 8 kg of hay

questions.title: Fleet Polymorphic Start
questions.description:
A fleet yard starts every vehicle the same way, yet each vehicle behaves differently underneath. Define base class Vehicle with a method start() that prints: Vehicle starting. Define Car, Bike and Truck subclasses, each overriding start() to print Car engine roaring, Bike engine purring and Truck engine rumbling respectively. Read n vehicles, park them in a Vehicle[] array, then start every vehicle from the array and print the yard summary.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n space-separated words, each Car, Bike or Truck.

Output Format:
One start line per vehicle in input order, then a final line: Cars: <c> Bikes: <b> Trucks: <t>.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100

questions.title: Shape Area Ranking Engine
questions.description:
A scoreboard ranks shapes by area. Define an abstract class Shape with an abstract method area(), plus Circle (field radius) and Rectangle (fields width, height). Read n shapes, compute each area through its Shape reference, sort the areas from largest to smallest with your own loop (no library sort), and print the ranking.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by the n shape descriptions, each written as circle r or rect w h, in order.

Output Format:
Print n lines: Rank <i>: <area with 2 decimals>, largest area first.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 < r, w, h <= 10000
